title: Bachelor's Degree
summary: Four years of undergraduate study in China, taught in Chinese or English, with a route from foundation or language year if you need it.
overview: A Chinese bachelor's degree usually takes four years, with medicine, architecture and some engineering programs running five. English-taught degrees are growing, especially in business, computer science and engineering, but the widest choice remains Chinese-taught.

Entry requirements depend on your school certificate, transcript and language level. Some universities accept students directly after high school; others require a foundation year or HSK 4–5. We map the actual requirement for each program and build a shortlist with realistic, ambitious and safer options.
fitFor: You have completed secondary school or will graduate this year
You want a full undergraduate degree in China
You are choosing between Chinese-taught and English-taught routes
You need a clear budget for four years, not just the first semester
outcomes: A recognised undergraduate degree from a Chinese university
Chinese language skills built alongside your major
Internship and graduate-study options in China
A four-year budget and scholarship plan agreed upfront

timeline.text: We define the major, language route and budget, then shortlist universities with the right entry rules.
Documents, translations, language certificates and motivation letters are prepared and checked.
Applications are submitted, interviews and entrance exams completed, offers compared.
Deposit, JW202, visa, housing and arrival planning. Registration dates are confirmed with the university.

faq.question: Can I study a bachelor's in English in China?
faq.answer: Yes, at selected universities and in selected majors, most often business, computer science, engineering and international studies. The catalogue is smaller than for Chinese-taught programs and changes each year.

faq.question: Do I need HSK for an English-taught degree?
faq.answer: Usually not for admission, but some universities require basic Chinese by graduation. We confirm the language rule for each program rather than assuming.
